model_annotation: Figure 2, titled "Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MISTRAL-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data," is a grouped bar chart that compares the average negative log-probabilities for tokens categorized into six different clinical specialties. The chart displays data for two models: the base model (MISTRAL-v0.2-base) and the model fine-tuned on each specialty (MISTRAL-v0.2-fine-tuned on...). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents the "Negative log probability" on a linear scale, ranging from 23 to 27. For each specialty, two bars are shown: a lighter-colored bar for the base model and a darker-colored bar for the fine-tuned model. The data shows that for all six specialties, the negative log-probability for the fine-tuned model is lower than for the base model, indicating a decrease in the average negative log-probability for tokens from the respective specialty. The lowest negative log-probability for the base model is 47.5 (Neuro), and the highest is 54.8 (Gastro). For the fine-tuned models, the lowest value is 41.9 (Infect) and the highest is 54.4 (Gastro). The chart visually confirms that fine-tuning reduces the negative log-probability for tokens from the specific specialty, suggesting the model has learned to assign higher probability to these tokens.
